title: Identifying Probability Localization Dynamics via Structured Stochastic Liftings
summary: This work develops a discrete-time framework for identifying probability localization dynamics through finite stochastic representations adapted in space, time, memory, and state information. A compact dynamically relevant set is localized by a finite measurable partition, producing an observable probability state and a relational graph of admissible transitions. Structured stochastic liftings derived from Stochastically Structured Reservoir Computing (SSRC) give lossless polynomial representations of the observable state, while stochastic delay liftings add finite observable memory.
